items.prompt:
Find and correct ALL errors in this paragraph excerpt.
'last halloween, my sister and i went to the rocky mountains with aunt sue. she brought a bag of snickers candy. its my sisters favorite holiday.'

List each error and write the corrected paragraph.
items.answer: Errors: 'last' at sentence start should be 'Last'; 'halloween' → 'Halloween' (holiday); 'i' → 'I' (pronoun); 'rocky mountains' → 'Rocky Mountains' (geographic name); 'aunt sue' → 'Aunt Sue' (title + name); 'snickers' → 'Snickers' (product/brand name); 'its' → 'It's' (contraction of 'it is'); 'sisters' → 'sister's' (possessive). Corrected: 'Last Halloween, my sister and I went to the Rocky Mountains with Aunt Sue. She brought a bag of Snickers candy. It's my sister's favorite holiday.'

steps: 'aunt sue' → 'Aunt Sue' (title used as part of name).
'sisters' → 'sister's' (possessive: the holiday that belongs to the sister).

items.prompt:
Rewrite this letter, correcting ALL errors in capitalization, punctuation (commas), and apostrophes.

'dear grandma
Thank you for the lego set you sent for christmas. its my favorite gift! I built it myself.
your grandson
mark'
items.answer:
Dear Grandma,
Thank you for the Lego set you sent for Christmas. It's my favorite gift! I built it myself.
Your grandson,
Mark

steps: Greeting: 'dear grandma' → 'Dear Grandma,' (comma after greeting; capitalize 'Grandma' as name).
Closing: 'your grandson' → 'Your grandson,' (comma after closing; 'your' starts closing so capitalize it).

items.prompt:
Find THREE errors in this paragraph and rewrite it correctly.
'The students science projects were displayed at the Jefferson museum. Ms. rodriguez said its the best show shes seen in years. She visited the museum on memorial day.'
items.answer: Errors: 'students science projects' → 'students' science projects' (plural possessive — the projects belonging to multiple students); 'rodriguez' → 'Rodriguez' (proper name, always capitalized); 'its' → 'it's' (contraction of 'it is'); 'shes' → 'she's' (contraction of 'she is'); 'memorial day' → 'Memorial Day' (holiday). Corrected: 'The students' science projects were displayed at the Jefferson museum. Ms. Rodriguez said it's the best show she's seen in years. She visited the museum on Memorial Day.'

steps: 'students science projects' — missing apostrophe for plural possession: students'.

items.prompt:
Read the student's draft and fix ALL capitalization and punctuation errors.

'dear mrs. kim
This summer my family visited niagara falls and ate breakfast at the ihop near our hotel. i loved the pancakes! my mom said its the best trip weve ever taken.
love
priya'
items.answer:

This summer my family visited Niagara Falls and ate breakfast at the IHOP near our hotel. I loved the pancakes! My mom said it's the best trip we've ever taken.

steps: Greeting: 'dear mrs. kim' → 'Dear Mrs. Kim,' (comma after greeting).

items.prompt: Explain the difference between 'their,' 'there,' and 'they're.' Write one original sentence correctly using each word.
items.answer: 'Their' = belonging to them (possessive pronoun). 'There' = at that place / to introduce a statement. 'They're' = they are (contraction). Sample sentences: 'Their dog loves to run.' / 'There is a bird on the fence.' / 'They're going to the library after lunch.'

steps: 'there' — refers to a place or introduces a sentence ('There is...').
Common mistake: using 'their' where 'they're' is needed, or 'there' where 'their' is needed.

items.prompt:
Rewrite this sentence correcting ALL three errors.
'The boys backpacks were left at yellowstone national park during there trip.'
Error 1: _____  Error 2: _____  Error 3: _____
Corrected sentence: _____
items.answer: Error 1: 'boys backpacks' → 'boys' backpacks' (plural possessive — apostrophe after 'boys'). Error 2: 'yellowstone national park' → 'Yellowstone National Park' (geographic name). Error 3: 'there trip' → 'their trip' ('there' refers to a place; 'their' shows possession). Corrected: 'The boys' backpacks were left at Yellowstone National Park during their trip.'

steps: Plural possessive: multiple boys each had backpacks → boys' backpacks (apostrophe after the -s).
Geographic name: 'Yellowstone National Park' is a proper noun — all words capitalized.
Homophones: 'their' shows possession ('their trip'), not 'there' (a place).

items.prompt:
A student wrote: 'We wont be able to go too the fourth of july parade because its raining.'
Find ALL errors and rewrite the sentence correctly.
items.answer: Errors: 'wont' → 'won't' (contraction of 'will not' — missing apostrophe); 'too' → 'to' (wrong word — 'too' means 'also' or 'excessively'; 'to' is the preposition needed); 'fourth of july' → 'Fourth of July' (holiday name, proper noun); 'its' → 'it's' (contraction of 'it is'). Corrected: 'We won't be able to go to the Fourth of July parade because it's raining.'

steps: 'too' → 'to' (wrong homophone — 'too' means also; 'to' is the preposition).
'fourth of july' → 'Fourth of July' (specific holiday — proper noun).

items.prompt:
Read the paragraph. Find and correct FOUR errors (capitalization, apostrophes, or commas in letter format).

'my teacher, ms. park, asked us to write letters to our pen pals for valentines day. I wrote:

dear Ana
I hope youre doing well. my family just moved near lake ontario. its beautiful here.
Your friend
ben'
items.answer:
Errors: 'my teacher' → 'My teacher' (start of sentence); 'valentines day' → 'Valentine's Day' (holiday with apostrophe, plus capitalized); letter greeting: 'dear Ana' → 'Dear Ana,' (comma after greeting); 'youre' → 'you're' (contraction of 'you are'); 'my family' → 'My family' (start of sentence); 'lake ontario' → 'Lake Ontario' (geographic name); 'its' → 'It's' (contraction of 'it is'); letter closing: 'Your friend' → 'Your friend,' (comma after closing); 'ben' → 'Ben' (proper name). Corrected paragraph: 'My teacher, Ms. Park, asked us to write letters to our pen pals for Valentine's Day. I wrote:

Dear Ana,
I hope you're doing well. My family just moved near Lake Ontario. It's beautiful here.
Your friend,
Ben'

steps: 'valentines day' → 'Valentine's Day' (holiday name capitalized; apostrophe in Valentine's).
Letter greeting: 'dear Ana' → 'Dear Ana,' (comma after name).

items.prompt:
Use the spelling pattern to write the word, then write a sentence using it.
(a) Base: 'hope' + -ful + -ness = _____ (state of being full of hope). Write a sentence.
(b) Base: 'nation' — related word using -al + -ity = nationality. Now write 'nation' + -al = _____ . Write a sentence.
items.answer: (a) hopefulness. Sample sentence: 'The children felt hopefulness as they waited for news.' (b) national. Sample sentence: 'We sang the national anthem at the game.'

steps: (a) hope → hopeful → hopefulness. The suffix -ness is added to the adjective 'hopeful' to form the noun 'hopefulness.'
(b) nation + -al = national. The suffix -al forms an adjective meaning 'relating to a nation'.

items.prompt:
Rewrite this sentence, fixing EVERY error.
'On new years day, the williams familys dog ran outside and barked at its own shadow; it's paws were muddy.'

List each error and write the corrected sentence.
items.answer: Errors: 'new years day' → 'New Year's Day' (holiday name + apostrophe showing New Year's); 'williams familys dog' → 'Williams family's dog' (possessive of proper noun Williams family); 'its own shadow' — 'its' here is correct (possessive); 'it's paws' → 'its paws' ('it's' = 'it is,' but here we need the possessive 'its'). Corrected: 'On New Year's Day, the Williams family's dog ran outside and barked at its own shadow; its paws were muddy.'

steps: 'new years day' → 'New Year's Day' — holiday name (proper noun) + apostrophe in 'New Year's.'
'williams familys' → 'Williams family's' — proper name capitalized; family + 's for singular possessive.
'its own shadow' — 'its' (possessive, no apostrophe) is correct here.
'it's paws' → 'its paws' — 'its' (no apostrophe) is the possessive form; 'it's' means 'it is'.

items.prompt:
A student wrote this closing for a letter. Find and fix all errors.
'your friend forever
jessica'

What two errors appear in this closing?
items.answer:
Errors: 'your friend forever' → 'Your friend forever,' (capitalize 'Your' at start of closing; add comma after 'forever'); 'jessica' → 'Jessica' (proper name always capitalized). Corrected closing: 'Your friend forever,
Jessica'

steps: The first word of a letter closing is capitalized: 'Your.'
A comma follows the last word of the closing: 'Your friend forever,'
The writer's name is a proper noun: 'Jessica.'

items.prompt:
Read the sentence. There are THREE errors. Find and fix them all.
'The childrens doctor said its important to brush you're teeth twice a day.'

Error 1: _____  Error 2: _____  Error 3: _____
Corrected sentence: _____
items.answer: Error 1: 'childrens' → 'children's' (possessive — the doctor belonging to the children; needs apostrophe before -s since 'children' is already the irregular plural). Error 2: 'its' → 'it's' (contraction of 'it is'). Error 3: 'you're' → 'your' ('you're' = 'you are'; here we need the possessive 'your'). Corrected: 'The children's doctor said it's important to brush your teeth twice a day.'

steps: 'childrens' → 'children's' — 'children' is the irregular plural; add 's for possessive.
'you're' → 'your' — the teeth belong to you; 'your' is possessive. 'You're' would mean 'you are,' which does not fit.

items.prompt:
A student used an apostrophe where none was needed. Identify the error and fix it.
'The dog's ran across the yard.'
What is wrong? Write the corrected sentence.
items.answer: The error is the apostrophe in 'dog's.' Here we are talking about more than one dog (the subject of 'ran'), so we need the plural 'dogs,' not the possessive 'dog's.' Corrected: 'The dogs ran across the yard.'

steps: 'dog's' with an apostrophe is a possessive — it means 'belonging to the dog.'
The sentence means multiple dogs ran — that requires the plural 'dogs' (no apostrophe).
An apostrophe is NEVER used just to make a plural.

items.prompt:
Write each contraction and then explain what letters the apostrophe replaces.
(a) I + will = _____   (b) could + not = _____   (c) she + would = _____   (d) have + not = _____
items.answer: (a) I'll — apostrophe replaces 'wi' in 'will.' (b) couldn't — apostrophe replaces 'o' in 'not.' (c) she'd — apostrophe replaces 'woul' in 'would.' (d) haven't — apostrophe replaces 'o' in 'not.'

steps: (a) I + will → I'll (wi is replaced by the apostrophe).
(b) could + not → couldn't (o in 'not' is replaced).
(c) she + would → she'd (woul is replaced by the apostrophe).
(d) have + not → haven't (o in 'not' is replaced).

items.prompt:
Read the paragraph. List every error and rewrite it correctly.
'Last spring, our class took a field trip to the smithsonian museum in washington dc. It was located near the potomac river. Ms. chen said its one of the most famous museums in the world. We saw exhibits about the wright brothers airplane.'

Find all capitalization, apostrophe, and possessive errors.
items.answer: Errors: 'smithsonian museum' → 'Smithsonian Museum' (proper name of institution); 'washington dc' → 'Washington, D.C.' (proper geographic name, standard abbreviation); 'potomac river' → 'Potomac River' (proper geographic name); 'its' → 'it's' (contraction of 'it is'); 'wright brothers airplane' → 'Wright brothers' airplane' (possessive — the airplane belonging to the Wright brothers; also 'Wright' should be capitalized as a proper name). Corrected: 'Last spring, our class took a field trip to the Smithsonian Museum in Washington, D.C. It was located near the Potomac River. Ms. Chen said it's one of the most famous museums in the world. We saw exhibits about the Wright brothers' airplane.'

steps: 'its' → 'it's' (it is one of the most famous).
'wright brothers airplane' → 'Wright brothers' airplane' (proper name 'Wright' capitalized; plural possessive 'brothers'' for the airplane belonging to the brothers).
